## Motivation

MLU CI is not registered with the shared slash-command interface introduced in #45735. Register it so contributors can label and rerun MLU CI through the existing commands and permissions.

## Modifications

- Add `mlu` to the opt-in tier registry, mapping `run-ci-mlu` to `pr-test-mlu.yml`.
- Enable `/tag-run-ci-label mlu` to add both required labels, `/tag-and-rerun-ci mlu` to label and retry unsuccessful workflows through the existing broad retry path, and `/run-ci mlu` or `/run-mlu-ci` to rerun MLU only, including successful runs.
- Scope `pull_request_target` rerun selection to the PR source repository and branch in addition to its head SHA.
- Use the shared live-label gate for MLU, removing the separate opt-in precheck and `labeled` trigger. Runs blocked by missing labels can be retried after labeling.
- Update the contribution guide, workflow README, and CI workflow skill with the MLU registration and rerun behavior.

## Validation

- Pre-commit and opt-in tier/workflow consistency checks passed.
- Mintlify broken-link check passed.

@@ -149,7 +149,7 @@ For CI to run on a pull request, it must have the "run-ci" label. Authorized use
 - `/run-ci nv` (also `/run-base-ci nv`, `/run-nv-ci`): Adds "run-ci" and reruns only NVIDIA base and shared checks, including successful runs. It does not select extra CI or other hardware. Only existing runs for the current commit are selected; workflows with no run are skipped. Existing hardware labels are kept, and future pushes follow the existing workflow gates.
 - `/run-full-ci`: Baseline **and** extra CI. Short form of `/tag-and-rerun-ci extra` — applies both labels, then reruns everything at the current commit that didn't succeed.
 - `/run-<tier>-ci`: One opt-in tier **only**, e.g. `/run-extra-ci`. Applies "run-ci" and the tier's optional label, then reruns just the listed workflows (including ones that already succeeded). Use `/run-extra-ci` when baseline is already green and you only need the shared extra tier.
-- `/run-extra-ci <hardware>` (also `/rerun-extra-ci <hardware>`): Equivalent to `/run-<hardware>-extra-ci` when that tier is registered. Otherwise, the suffix keeps its existing behavior and is ignored. The `extra` tier covers **both NVIDIA and AMD extra CI** using the existing shared "run-ci-extra" label; `/run-extra-ci amd` therefore still runs that shared tier. Hardware extra tiers will be split separately. The `nv` selection covers NVIDIA base and shared checks only. Hardware-specific tier commands such as `/run-amd-ci`, `/run-ppu-ci`, and `/run-mlu-ci` are not registered.
+- `/run-extra-ci <hardware>` (also `/rerun-extra-ci <hardware>`): Equivalent to `/run-<hardware>-extra-ci` when that tier is registered. Otherwise, the suffix keeps its existing behavior and is ignored. The `extra` tier covers **both NVIDIA and AMD extra CI** using the existing shared "run-ci-extra" label; `/run-extra-ci amd` therefore still runs that shared tier. Hardware extra tiers will be split separately. The `nv` selection covers NVIDIA base and shared checks only. The `mlu` tier is registered for `/run-ci mlu` and `/run-mlu-ci`. Other hardware-specific tier commands such as `/run-amd-ci` and `/run-ppu-ci` are not registered.
 - `/rerun-test <test-spec> [<test-spec> ...]`: Reruns one or more specific tests directly. A spec may select a file, class, or method using `<file>::<TestClass>[.<test_method>]`. Multiple specs and file globs are supported. `--changed` (short form `-c`) adds every test file the PR itself adds or modifies (under `test/registered/` or the multimodal test directory), so a PR that touches several tests can rerun them all without listing them. Examples: `/rerun-test test_srt_endpoint.py`, `/rerun-test registered/core/test_srt_endpoint.py::TestSRTEndpoint.test_simple_decode`, `/rerun-test test_a.py test_b.py`, `/rerun-test test_*backend*.py`, `/rerun-test --changed`, or `/rerun-test -c`.
 - `/rerun-group <group> [<group> ...]`: Expands one or more registered test groups (for example, `/rerun-group rust-server`) and dispatches their tests through the same selective-rerun workflow. Groups are defined in [`scripts/ci/rerun_test_groups.json`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/scripts/ci/rerun_test_groups.json).
 - `/run-cpu-ci`: Runs only the CPU unit suite (`base-a-test-cpu`) against the PR head, partitioned the same way as in PR CI, without the `run-ci` label or any GPU stage. For a small PR, `/run-cpu-ci` plus `/rerun-group <module>` covers the unit tests and the affected module's tests. Alias: `/rerun-cpu-ci`.
